flow-and-order.label: Flow and order
flow-and-order.description: What happens in which order: steps, messages, moments in time, and loops

structure-and-containment.label: Structure and containment
structure-and-containment.description: How parts are built up: levels, hierarchies, boundaries, and connections

comparison.label: Comparison
comparison.description: How things differ or correspond: options, a change, two measures, and matching entries

state-and-change.label: State and change
state-and-change.description: How something moves on: states, decisions, amounts over time, and a person's path

process-flow.label: Process flow
process-flow.shows: The order of steps that turn an input into a result, answering what happens first, next, and last.
process-flow.parts: Steps drawn as boxes or stations, arrows that carry the output of one step into the next, and the input and the result at the two ends.
process-flow.reading_order: Start at the input and follow the arrows step by step to the result, left to right or top to bottom.
process-flow.fits: A pipeline, a build or deploy procedure, a request handled in several stages, or any work done in a fixed order.
process-flow.misfits: Exchanges between several actors, which a message sequence shows, and steps that repeat without an end, which a cycle shows.

message-sequence.label: Message sequence
message-sequence.shows: Who sends what to whom and in which order, answering how several actors talk to finish one task.
message-sequence.parts: One vertical lifeline per actor, horizontal arrows for the messages labeled with what they carry, and the replies drawn back between the same lifelines.
message-sequence.reading_order: Read from top to bottom; each arrow happens after the arrows above it.
message-sequence.fits: Calls between a client and its servers, a sign-in or payment handshake, and messages between services.
message-sequence.misfits: Work one actor does alone, which a process flow shows, and long spans of calendar time, which a timeline shows.

timeline.label: Timeline
timeline.shows: When events happened along one time axis, answering what came before what and how far apart.
timeline.parts: A single time axis with marked points or spans, each labeled with its date or moment and its event.
timeline.reading_order: Follow the axis from the earliest point to the latest.
timeline.fits: Release histories, incidents, project milestones, and the history of one value.
timeline.misfits: Steps whose durations do not matter, which a process flow shows, and amounts that rise and fall, which a quantity trend shows.

cycle.label: Cycle
cycle.shows: Stages that repeat and come back to the start, answering what keeps the loop going.
cycle.parts: Stages placed around a ring, arrows that run one way around it, and the arrow that closes the loop back to the first stage.
cycle.reading_order: Start at the marked first stage and go around the ring in the direction of the arrows until you are back at the start.
cycle.fits: Feedback loops, release cycles, retry loops, and plan, do, check, act.
cycle.misfits: Work with a clear end, which a process flow shows, and states that move between each other in many directions, which a state machine shows.

layers.label: Layers
layers.shows: Which level sits on which and what each level relies on below it, answering where a part belongs in a stack.
layers.parts: Horizontal bands stacked from the lowest level to the highest, each band named, with the interface between neighbors marked on their shared edge.
layers.reading_order: Read from the bottom band up to see what builds on what, or from the top down to see what a request passes through.
layers.fits: Network protocol stacks, the layers of a software architecture, and levels of abstraction.
layers.misfits: Groups that contain each other, which nesting shows, and parts that connect in many directions, which a network shows.

tree.label: Tree
tree.shows: How one root branches into children and their descendants, answering what belongs under what in a hierarchy.
tree.parts: A root node, child nodes below or beside it, and lines that join each parent to its children.
tree.reading_order: Start at the root and follow one branch down to the leaf you are looking for.
tree.fits: Folder structures, organization charts, class hierarchies, and breakdowns into categories.
tree.misfits: Elements with more than one parent or with loops, which a network shows, and boundaries drawn inside boundaries, which nesting shows.

nesting.label: Nesting
nesting.shows: Which boundary sits inside which, answering what is contained in what and where its limits lie.
nesting.parts: Enclosures drawn inside larger enclosures, each with its name on its edge, and the items placed inside the boundary they belong to.
nesting.reading_order: Read from the outermost boundary inward, or find an item and read outward through the boundaries around it.
nesting.fits: Scopes in code, permissions within an organization, containers on a host, and sets within sets.
nesting.misfits: A strict order of levels, which layers show, and branching from a single root, which a tree shows.

network.label: Network
network.shows: Which elements connect to which without a single root or order, answering how the parts reach each other.
network.parts: Nodes placed near the nodes they relate to, and links between them, labeled when a link has a kind or a direction.
network.reading_order: Start at the node in question, follow its links to its neighbors, and go on to the nodes they reach.
network.fits: Maps of service dependencies, peer-to-peer networks, social graphs, and maps of related ideas.
network.misfits: A single hierarchy, which a tree shows, and an exchange whose order matters, which a message sequence shows.

side-by-side.label: Side by side
side-by-side.shows: How two or more options differ on the same points, answering which option does what.
side-by-side.parts: One column or panel per option, with the same points in the same places in every panel so that equal points line up.
side-by-side.reading_order: Read one point across the panels to compare the options on it, then move down to the next point.
side-by-side.fits: Comparing libraries, plans, protocols, or approaches on the same criteria.
side-by-side.misfits: One thing at two moments, which a before and after shows, and options placed by two measures, which a two-axis matrix shows.

before-after.label: Before and after
before-after.shows: What one thing looks like before a change and after it, answering what the change altered.
before-after.parts: Two panels of the same subject drawn the same way, the before on the left and the after on the right, with the changed parts marked.
before-after.reading_order: Read the before panel, then the after panel, and look at the marked differences.
before-after.fits: Refactorings, migrations, changes of configuration, and fixes.
before-after.misfits: Several options with no order between them, which side by side shows, and many moments in a row, which a timeline shows.

two-axis-matrix.label: Two-axis matrix
two-axis-matrix.shows: Where items fall on two measures at once, answering which items are high or low on each measure.
two-axis-matrix.parts: Two crossing axes with their names and directions, the quadrants or cells they make, and the items placed by their two values.
two-axis-matrix.reading_order: Read the names of the two axes first, then find each item and the quadrant it falls in.
two-axis-matrix.fits: Priorities by impact and effort, trade-offs between cost and speed, and the positions of competing options.
two-axis-matrix.misfits: Options compared point by point instead of placed, which side by side shows, and exact pairs of entries, which a correspondence table shows.

correspondence-table.label: Correspondence table
correspondence-table.shows: Which entry on one side matches which entry on the other, answering what maps to what.
correspondence-table.parts: Two lists, or a grid of rows and columns, with each matching pair on one row or joined by one line.
correspondence-table.reading_order: Find an entry on one side and read across its row or along its line to the entry it matches.
correspondence-table.fits: Mappings between terms, the fields of two formats, old and new names, and permissions by role.
correspondence-table.misfits: Items placed by two continuous measures, which a two-axis matrix shows, and a change over time, which a before and after or a timeline shows.

state-machine.label: State machine
state-machine.shows: Which states something can be in and which events move it between them, answering what can happen next from here.
state-machine.parts: States drawn as rounded nodes, arrows between them labeled with the event or condition that causes each transition, and the start and end states marked.
state-machine.reading_order: Start at the initial state and follow the arrow of the event that occurs to the next state.
state-machine.fits: The status of an order or a payment, connection states, document workflows, and the lifecycle of a transaction.
state-machine.misfits: Work that always runs in one order, which a process flow shows, and a single choice made once, which a decision branch shows.

decision-branch.label: Decision branch
decision-branch.shows: Which path follows from each answer to a question or a condition, answering what to do in a given case.
decision-branch.parts: Questions or conditions drawn as decision points, one labeled branch per answer, and the outcomes at the ends of the branches.
decision-branch.reading_order: Start at the first question, take the branch that matches your case, and go on until you reach an outcome.
decision-branch.fits: Troubleshooting guides, choosing an option by its conditions, access checks, and the paths of error handling.
decision-branch.misfits: States that the same thing returns to, which a state machine shows, and a hierarchy of parts, which a tree shows.

quantity-trend.label: Quantity trend
quantity-trend.shows: How an amount rises and falls across time or another measure, answering how big it is and which way it is heading.
quantity-trend.parts: A horizontal axis of time or another measure, a vertical axis of the amount with its unit, and a line, bars, or points for the values.
quantity-trend.reading_order: Read the axes and their units first, then follow the values from left to right and note where they turn.
quantity-trend.fits: Latency across releases, costs by month, growth in usage, and the effect of a change on a number.
quantity-trend.misfits: Events without amounts, which a timeline shows, and values with no order along the horizontal axis, which side by side shows.

journey-map.label: Journey map
journey-map.shows: What a person does, meets, and feels at each stage of using something, answering where the experience goes well or breaks.
journey-map.parts: Stages along the top in the order a person meets them, rows under each stage for the actions, the touchpoints, and the feelings, and marks where trouble occurs.
journey-map.reading_order: Read the stages from left to right, and at each stage read down the rows to see the action, the touchpoint, and the feeling.
journey-map.fits: Onboarding, a purchase from search to delivery, contacts with support, and how a developer adopts a tool.
journey-map.misfits: The inside of a system with no person in it, which a process flow or a message sequence shows, and a single event at one moment.
